interest: This file provides valuable historical insight into U.S.-Japan intellectual property disputes and cultural diplomacy during the 1930s, highlighting the severe legal limitations of the bilateral 1905 Copyright Convention, which left American works unprotected against unauthorized Japanese translations. It illustrates how Japanese publishers commercially exploited major American bestsellers—including W. Jefferson Davis's 'Japan — The Air Menace of the Pacific' (selling some 45,000 copies of an unauthorized translation), Margaret Mitchell's 'Gone With the Wind', and Dale Carnegie's 'How to Win Friends and Influence People'—as well as McGraw-Hill technical titles pirated in China and imported into Japan. For diplomatic and legal historians, the file reveals the State Department's internal policy debates, notably led by Dr. Wallace McClure, over using these high-profile infringement controversies to lobby for U.S. accession to the Berne Convention.
overview: This collection consists of the Department of State's docket index sheets ('List of Papers') for Decimal File 894.544, documenting U.S.-Japan relations regarding copyrights, intellectual property legislation, and unauthorized publications between 1931 and 1939. The file contains four distinct docket sections: the master general file register (pages 1–4) recording Japanese copyright enactments (notably Law No. 64 of 1931 amending Law No. 39), Japanese court decisions on international copyright protection under the Berne Convention and 1928 Rome Revision, and related diplomatic inquiries; and three specialized 'jacket case' registers tracking high-profile infringement controversies involving American authors and publishers. These jacket cases detail the unauthorized Japanese translation and mass sale of W. Jefferson Davis's book 'Japan — The Air Menace of the Pacific' (pages 5–7), legal inquiries regarding foreign translation rights for Margaret Mitchell's 'Gone With the Wind' (page 8), and the unauthorized importation and sale in Japan of Chinese-pirated McGraw-Hill textbooks and condensed American bestsellers such as Dale Carnegie's 'How to Win Friends and Influence People' (pages 9–10).

subfiles.about: Master docket register sheets recording State Department communications, Japanese statutes, court rulings, and diplomatic actions regarding copyright protection in Japan from 1931 to 1939.
subfiles.summary: This four-page docket list indexes official State Department communications filed under decimal number 894.544 between 1931 and 1939. It chronicles the promulgation of Japanese Law No. 64 of 1931 (revising Copyright Law No. 39), reports on Tokyo court rulings affecting foreign copyrights, and tracks U.S. diplomatic assessments regarding the Berne Convention and the 1928 Rome Revision. The entries also record extensive inter-agency consultations with the Library of Congress and Department of Commerce, inquiries from U.S. Senators Key Pittman and F. Ryan Duffy, and notices sent to prominent publishers and legal representatives regarding unauthorized Japanese publications.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Decimal File 894.544 (Copyrights - Japan)

subfiles.about: Jacket case docket register recording State Department investigations and diplomatic correspondence concerning the unauthorized Japanese translation and distribution of W. Jefferson Davis's book 'Japan — The Air Menace of the Pacific'.
keywords: Japan - The Air Menace of the Pacific
subfiles.summary: This three-page jacket case register documents the State Department's multi-year handling of complaints from author W. Jefferson Davis regarding the pirating of his book 'Japan — The Air Menace of the Pacific', which sold roughly 45,000 copies in unauthorized Japanese translation. Legal Adviser Ward and Treaty Division official Wallace McClure concluded that the bilateral Copyright Convention of 1905 afforded no protection for translation rights, leaving no formal basis for diplomatic protest and restricting recourse to Japanese courts. Subsequent entries trace discussions regarding potential Berne Convention coverage via Curtis Publishing Company serializations, inquiries by copyright attorney Stephen P. Ladas, and interviews in Tokyo by Counselor Eugene H. Dooman with publisher Ko Kawarada recommending an informal small settlement.
subfiles.title: Jacket Case List of Papers: Protection in Japan of Copyright Owned by W. Jefferson Davis

subfiles.about: Jacket case docket sheet recording an inquiry regarding foreign translation rights and Berne Convention protections in Japan for Margaret Mitchell's novel 'Gone With the Wind'.
subfiles.summary: This single-page docket register sheet contains a cross-reference entry regarding an inquiry submitted by attorney Walbridge S. Taft on August 11 concerning foreign translation rights for Margaret Mitchell's novel 'Gone With the Wind'. Taft sought advice on whether the book enjoyed protection under the Berne Convention in Japan and whether any other legal mechanisms existed to prevent unauthorized editions. The entry cross-references related files under decimal number 812.544.
subfiles.title: Jacket Case List of Papers: Foreign Translation Rights of Gone With the Wind

subfiles.about: Jacket case docket register recording correspondence and embassy investigations regarding the importation and sale in Japan of unauthorized Chinese pirated McGraw-Hill books and other American publications.
keywords: How to Win Friends and Influence People
subfiles.summary: This two-page jacket case register chronicles complaints submitted by Curtis McGraw of McGraw-Hill Book Company concerning unauthorized reprints pirated in China and imported for sale in Japan. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and the Tokyo Embassy investigated the matter through the Maruzen Company, confirming that sales were limited to a single bookseller and absent from general Tokyo retail channels. The docket also indexes reports on an unauthorized condensed Japanese edition of Dale Carnegie's 'How to Win Friends and Influence People' published in the periodical Fusi, as well as the Department's advice regarding the inadequacy of existing treaty protections.
subfiles.title: Jacket Case List of Papers: Infringement in Japan of Copyrights of McGraw-Hill Book Co., Inc.
